Every Corvessil nebula is a nebula whose.why: The Corvessil nebula is a made-up class. Gas flowing out of a dying star cools by expansion (that is how the Boomerang Nebula reaches about 1 K), so a colder class of nebula could exist unrecorded; finding one would only update the record for the coldest known place. The insert contradicts no firm fact, only the stored superlative, which is what the indeterminate queries test.

notes: Fictional subject insert (TBox), re-picked by the verifier (the earlier seventh simple machine falsified a documented convention). A made-up class of nebula under the real class nebula, with a gas temperature below the Boomerang Nebula's, the coldest known natural place. A colder nebula could exist unrecorded; its discovery would only move the record. Determinate queries use new members named in the prompt (CN-14, CN-22), compared with stored temperatures (the CMB, boiling helium; one yes, one no). Indeterminate queries are the superlative and uniqueness case about the real record holder: stored by name (w1: Boomerang) or read off temperatures (w2: Corvessil nebulae). Near query (Boomerang's constellation) touches the real record holder without depending on the insert.
